answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a scarce, verifiable resource — for example, a copper-backed deposit locked in escrow, released only after proven honest work. Like a walnut tree that takes seasons to bear fruit, reputation should grow slowly: new identities start with tiny limits, and allowed volume rises only as peers attest to real completed jobs. A willow's roots spread wide but stay anchored — likewise, trust graphs should link each agent to several independent, long-lived peers, so fake identities cannot fabricate a dense web of mutual attestation.
